notes:
Addressed every low finding from the review (the sole high finding was an external, already-resolved build break in another package's file, not in this package's scope):

1. (Test gap, WInput.razor.css contract) Added AdornedFieldCss_ReservesAdornmentTrack in WInputTests.cs — reads WInput.razor.css off disk via the existing FindRepoFile helper, isolates the `.w-field-control--adorned` rule, and asserts `padding-inline-end: 40px`, using the same pattern as the existing FieldControlCss_DeclaresUnicodeBidiPlaintext test. Also added FieldControlClass_IsAdorned_OnlyForDateAndPassword (Theory, 4 cases: Date/Password expect the class, Text/Number do not) locking the Blazor-side class list.

2. (Test gap, W08 tab badge) Added W08AttentionCenter_AllTabBadge_MatchesTodayActionCount in ShellTests.cs — renders W08AttentionCenter, reads the first `.w-tab`'s `.w-badge` text, and asserts it equals Ar.AttentionCenter.TodayActionCount.ToString(). Added `using Wakeel.Design.Text;` to ShellTests.cs for the Ar reference. W08AttentionCenter.razor itself already had the correct fix from the prior round (Count="Ar.AttentionCenter.TodayActionCount" on the «الكل» WTabItem) — untouched here, just newly locked by a test.

3. (Exception-swallowing scope, WInput.razor OnAfterRenderAsync) Widened the catch around the wakeelUi.setInputValue interop call from `catch (JSException)` to `catch (Exception ex) when (ex is JSException or JSDisconnectedException or ObjectDisposedException)`, per the finding — JSDisconnectedException/ObjectDisposedException don't derive from JSException, so a teardown race during the pending caret write could previously escape a lifecycle method and tear down the renderer. Microsoft.JSInterop is already imported via Wakeel.Design/_Imports.razor so both types resolve without a new using.

4. (Keystroke-ordering race, WInput.razor OnDateInputAsync) Added `private int _inputSeq;`, captured `var seq = ++_inputSeq;` at the top of OnDateInputAsync, and after the `await Js.InvokeAsync<int>("wakeelUi.getSelectionStart", ...)` added `if (seq != _inputSeq) { return; }` before stashing _pendingCaret/_pendingValue or invoking ValueChanged — so a keystroke whose interop round-trip is outrun by a later one no longer overwrites the newer pending state or emits a stale Value (the later call's raw e.Value already carries every digit typed so far, since the native input accumulates them, so no digit is lost by discarding the superseded call).

5. (Cosmetic class-string duplication, WInput.razor) Added a single `ControlClass` computed property (`Type is WInputType.Date or WInputType.Password ? "w-field-control w-field-control--adorned" : "w-field-control"`) and pointed both the Date and non-Date `<input>` elements at `class="@ControlClass"`, replacing the hardcoded literal on the Date branch and the ternary-with-trailing-space on the other, so the adorned-class rule is expressed once and Text/Number/error inputs no longer render a trailing space in their class attribute.
